Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 25 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученици Пелагија, Теодосија и Дула.“, where it is the second of the three names, with the rank words Свети мученици left off. attestations.note: The page heads her «(; - 361)» and gives the pair a single sentence of narrative: martyrdom at Caesarea in Palestine in the year 361, perfected by the sword. It prints the menaion's couplet for the two of them and no hymn. The two women share one life page, https://www.saint.gr/95/saint.aspx, whose «Ημερομηνία Εορτής» is the same 25 March.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.04.2026 (25. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Пелагија, Теодосија и Дула.“

attestations.note: The second name in the day's second entry, on the same menologion day the Greek already keeps in this folder, and the same woman: the Greek line here names two women together, «Αγίες Πελαγία και Θεοδοσία», and the Prologue heads the same two in the same order and says they were beheaded together with the sword after prison and torments. The third name on the Prologue's heading is a servant it says suffered alone and died at Nicomedia; she is the new folder `dula-of-nicomedia` in this same batch, and she takes no `related` row here, because the entry separates her from these two in its own words. The entry gives no year, no reign and no persecutor, so the 361 this folder already holds is untouched, and it names no city for these two either. The stored form is the bare forename, because Свети мученици stands at the head of the three and the heading gives this woman no epithet; Caesarea in Palestine is the corpus's own way of telling her from the other Theodosias and is nowhere on the Prologue's page. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr: «Οι Αγίες Μάρτυρες Πελαγία και Θεοδοσία, μαρτύρησαν στην Καισάρεια της Παλαιστίνης το έτος 361 μ.Χ. και τελειώθηκαν διά ξίφους», and the page heads her «(; - 361)», leaving the year of her birth a question mark.
